card.name: Sanjuanero
card.profile: A festive Colombian bambuco of Huila/Tolima tied to the San Pedro/San Juan festivities; the music was composed in 1936 by Anselmo Duran Plazas with lyrics by Sofia Gaitan Yanguas, first recorded in the 1950s by the duo Garzon y Collazos (Wikipedia). The traditional choreography, created by folklorist Ines Garcia de Duran in 1960, has three basic steps (caminado, bambuqueado, contradanza) and eight figures depicting courtship. Anthem of the Festival Folclorico y Reinado Nacional del Bambuco in Neiva.
card.insight: Though derived from bambuco with joropo influence, the Sanjuanero Huilense is widely considered Colombia's most representative folkloric dance and is the obligatory piece performed by contestants of the Reinado Nacional del Bambuco (Wikipedia; Gobernacion del Huila).
card.image_significance: The festive bambuco of Neiva. A representative image shows colorful regional costume and lively partner or troupe footwork — Huila/Tolima, Colombia.
